# Modern Web Guidance (Source) This repo is the source repository for [GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance) and includes the code and documentation for authoring, calibrating, and evaluating its contents. [**Modern Web Guidance**](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and [GOVERNANCE.md](./GOVERNANCE.md) for how we work on the project and orientation of the codebase. --- *Stewarded by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams, alongside the web development community.* [Documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/modern-web-guidance) · [Eval Dashboard](https://googlechrome.github.io/modern-web-guidance-src/) · [Source Code](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src) · [Report an Issue](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src/issues) ## Quickstart ```shell npx modern-web-guidance@latest install ``` This command runs an interactive wizard to install Modern Web Guidance. See [Alternative Installation Methods](#-alternative-installation-methods) below. #### Try it out (without installing) ```shell # Search for relevant guides npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "animate a dialog modal backdrop" # Retrieve a guide by ID npx modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "animate-to-from-top-layer" # Scan a codebase for legacy patterns to modernize npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan . ``` ## Why? Coding agents often default to older patterns because LLM training data contains vast amounts of legacy code. This often leads them to generate bloated JavaScript for tasks that now have native, high-performance web platform solutions. Even if a model knows an API exists, it often lacks the density of real-world, modern implementation patterns required for production-ready code. **Modern Web Guidance bridges this gap.** Our skill's CLI returns targeted, expert-curated guidelines directly into your agent's context window, focusing on: * **Modern Browser APIs**: Helping models correctly structure APIs they frequently misuse. * **Performance & Accessibility**: Preferring platform-level APIs that can be optimized by the browser and include built-in accessibility affordances. * **Responsible Fallbacks**: Guiding models to use sensible, lightweight fallbacks instead of heavy polyfills or legacy libraries. ## What's Included? We cover the past several years of the web platform's new features, all the way up to the cutting edge. The guides are **designed to be token-efficient**; we run evals enabling us to prune lowest-common-denominator content that models already know. ### Core Disciplines

🎨 User Experience

Smooth visual states (View Transitions, entry/exit animations, parallax scroll, CSS scrollbar-color).

📐 CSS Layout

Modern layout systems (container queries, subgrid, modern color spaces like oklch, text-wrap tuning, and line-height trimming).

⚡ Performance

Speed optimizations (instant preloading, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) diagnostics, and scheduling tasks via scheduler.yield).

📝 Forms & UI

Native components (Anchor Positioning for tooltips, Popover API, dialogs, :user-invalid validation, and auto-sizing fields).

♿ Accessibility

Important considerations (screen reader and keyboard operability, content navigation and discoverability).

🤖 Built-in AI

Local client models (native translation, summarization, and language detection APIs).
_View an example:_ [the `navigation-drawer` guide](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance/blob/main/skills/modern-web-guidance/guides/ui-components/navigation-drawer.md). #### The full list

# Sure: The personal finance app for everyone Get involved: [Discord](https://discord.gg/36ZGBsxYEK) • [Website](https://sure.am) • [Issues](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/issues) > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository is a community fork of the now-abandoned Maybe Finance project.
> Learn more in their [final release](https://github.com/maybe-finance/maybe/releases/tag/v0.6.0) doc. ## Backstory The [Maybe Finance](https://github.com/maybe-finance/maybe) (archived/abandoned repo) team spent most of 2021–2022 building a full-featured personal finance and wealth management app. It even included an “Ask an Advisor” feature that connected users with a real CFP/CFA — all included with your subscription. The business end of things didn't work out, and so they stopped developing the app in mid-2023. After spending nearly $1 million on development (employees, contractors, data providers, infra, etc.), the team open-sourced the app. Their goal was to let users self-host it for free — and eventually launch a hosted version for a small fee. They actually did launch that hosted version … briefly. That also didn’t work out — at least not as a sustainable B2C business — so now here we are: hosting a community-maintained fork to keep the codebase alive and see where this can go next. Join us! ## Hosting Sure Sure is a fully working personal finance app that can be [self hosted with Docker](docs/hosting/docker.md). Sure can be accessed from a browser, the macOS desktop app, the mobile app, API clients, and LLM agents. See [Sure Clients](docs/clients.md) for an overview. ## Forking and Attribution This repo is a community fork of the archived Maybe Finance repo. You’re free to fork it under the AGPLv3 license — but we’d love it if you stuck around and contributed here instead. To stay compliant and avoid trademark issues: - Be sure to include the original [AGPLv3 license](https://github.com/maybe-finance/maybe/blob/main/LICENSE) and clearly state in your README that your fork is based on Maybe Finance but is **not affiliated with or endorsed by** Maybe Finance Inc. - "Maybe" is a trademark of Maybe Finance Inc. and therefore, use of it is NOT allowed in forked repositories (or the logo) ## Performance Issues With data-heavy apps, inevitably, there are performance issues. We've set up a public dashboard showing the problematic requests seen on the demo site, along with the stacktraces to help debug them. [https://www.skylight.io/app/applications/s6PEZSKwcklL/recent/6h/endpoints](https://oss.skylight.io/app/applications/s6PEZSKwcklL/recent/6h/endpoints) Any contributions that help improve performance are very much welcome. ## Local Development Setup **If you are trying to _self-host_ the app, [read this guide to get started](docs/hosting/docker.md).** The instructions below are for developers to get started with contributing to the app. ### Requirements - See `.ruby-version` file for required Ruby version - PostgreSQL >9.3 (latest stable version recommended) - Redis > 5.4 (latest stable version recommended) ### Getting Started ```sh cd sure cp .env.local.example .env.local bin/setup bin/dev # Optionally, load demo data rake demo_data:default ``` Visit http://localhost:3000 to view the app. If you loaded the optional demo data, log in with these credentials: - Email: `user@example.com` - Password: `Password1!` For further instructions, see guides below. ### Setup Guides - [Mac dev setup](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/wiki/Mac-Dev-Setup-Guide) - [Linux dev setup](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/wiki/Linux-Dev-Setup-Guide) - [Windows dev setup](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/wiki/Windows-Dev-Setup-Guide) - Dev containers - visit [this guide](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/devcontainers/containers) ### One-click Install Render expects each button target branch to have a `render.yaml` at the repository root. The branch-ready Blueprint files live in `branches//render.yaml` in a separate repo and can be copied to each corresponding branch root. | Option | What it deploys | `latest` | `stable` | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Sure - No AI** | Sure web, Sidekiq worker, Render Postgres, and Render Key Value. AI tokens are intentionally blank. | [![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy?repo=https://github.com/we-promise/sure-render-templates/tree/sure-no-ai-latest) | [![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy?repo=https://github.com/we-promise/sure-render-templates/tree/sure-no-ai) | | **Sure - Simple AI** | Sure with OpenAI-backed AI settings, pgvector-ready Postgres, Sidekiq, and Render Key Value. Render prompts for the OpenAI token. | [![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy?repo=https://github.com/we-promise/sure-render-templates/tree/sure-simple-ai-latest) | [![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy?repo=https://github.com/we-promise/sure-render-templates/tree/sure-simple-ai) | | **Sure - External AI** | Sure with external assistant settings plus AlphaClaw, which manages the OpenClaw gateway on Render. | [![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy?repo=https://github.com/we-promise/sure-render-templates/tree/sure-external-ai-latest) | [![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy?repo=https://github.com/we-promise/sure-render-templates/tree/sure-external-ai) | [![Run on PikaPods](https://www.pikapods.com/static/run-button.svg)](https://www.pikapods.com/pods?run=sure) [![Deploy on Hostim](https://hostim.dev/img/deploy-button.svg)](https://console.hostim.dev/dashboard?preview=1&modal=1&template=sure) ## License and Trademarks Maybe and Sure are both distributed under an [AGPLv3 license](https://github.com/we-promise/sure/blob/main/LICENSE). - "Maybe" is a trademark of Maybe Finance, Inc. - "Sure" is not, and refers to this community fork.

name: free-claude-code
description: Use Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, VSCode, Pi, and OpenCode (and 6 other harnesses) for free (1.3B+ free tokens) from your terminal, app, IDE, or phone, and now from the browser with native browser sessions (multi-harness + multi-model) like OpenClaw (voice supported + ToS friendly)
readme_content:
[![License: AGPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-AGPL_v3-2e7d32.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/Alishahryar1/free-claude-code/blob/main/LICENSE) [![Python 3.14](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.14-3776ab.svg?style=for-the-badge&logo=python&logoColor=white)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![Package Manager: uv](assets/package-manager-uv.svg)](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) [![Testing: Pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/Testing-Pytest-ad1457.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/Alishahryar1/free-claude-code/actions/workflows/tests.yml) [![Type Checker: Ty](https://img.shields.io/badge/Type%20Checker-ty-fdd835.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://pypi.org/project/ty/) [![Formatter: Ruff](https://img.shields.io/badge/Formatter-ruff-bf4b00.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![Logging: Loguru](https://img.shields.io/badge/logging-loguru-00695c.svg?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/Delgan/loguru) [Quick Start](#quick-start) · [Providers](#choose-a-provider) · [Clients](#connect-your-client) · [Integrations](#optional-integrations) · [Manage](#manage-your-installation)

Independent open-source project. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic. Claude and Claude Code are trademarks of Anthropic.

## Features - Route any supported harness to models from any supported provider. - 12 supported harnesses: [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview), [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex), [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi), [OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode), [Cline](https://github.com/cline/cline), [Hermes](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent), [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), [Grok Build](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build), [Muse Code](https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-code-and-muse-spark-1-2/), [Aider](https://aider.chat/), [Antigravity CLI](https://antigravity.google/docs/getting-started/), or [VS Code Chat](https://code.visualstudio.com/). - Preserved native streaming, tool use, and interleaved thinking for maximum performance. - For Claude Code, route [Fable](https://www.anthropic.com/claude/fable), [Opus](https://www.anthropic.com/claude/opus), [Sonnet](https://www.anthropic.com/claude/sonnet), and [Haiku](https://www.anthropic.com/claude/haiku) to supported models. - 61 supported providers, including free, paid, subscription, and local providers. - 1.3B+ free tokens per month. - FCC follows provider TOS and removes integrations if they stop being allowed. - Use through the terminal, desktop apps ([Codex App](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app), [Claude Desktop](https://claude.ai/download), and [DeepSeek Desktop](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)), IDE extensions ([VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) and [JetBrains](https://www.jetbrains.com/)), your phone ([Discord](https://discord.com/) and [Telegram](https://telegram.org/)), or your browser through native Code sessions. - Voice notes supported for Discord and Telegram using local [Whisper](https://github.com/openai/whisper) or [NVIDIA NIM](https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/speech/latest/asr/deploy-asr-models/whisper.html). - Up to 90% lower token usage using [RTK](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk) and [Headroom](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom). - State-of-the-art reliability features so you can keep coding through provider outages: - Automatic retries. - Configurable rate limits. - Configurable concurrency control. - Automatic model/provider fallback. - Automatic multi-API key fallback. Free-tier availability and limits are controlled by each provider and may change.

Claude Code running with FCC.

A native Codex session in FCC's browser UI.

## Quick Start ### 1. Install macOS/Linux: ```bash curl -fsSL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Alishahryar1/free-claude-code/main/scripts/install.sh" | sh ``` Windows PowerShell: ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Alishahryar1/free-claude-code/main/scripts/install.ps1"))) ``` When prompted, choose at least one coding agent and optionally enable [RTK](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk) + [Headroom](https://github.com/headroomlabs-ai/headroom) token optimization for supported agents. ### 2. Start FCC #### Windows Open **Free Claude Code** from your desktop or Start menu. #### macOS Open **Free Claude Code** from your desktop or Applications folder. #### Linux Run: ```bash fcc-server ``` FCC opens the Admin UI after starting. On Windows and macOS, use the tray or menu-bar icon to open Admin, restart, or quit. When using `fcc-server`, keep its terminal open. ### 3. Configure NVIDIA NIM 1. Create an API key at [build.nvidia.com/settings/api-keys](https://build.nvidia.com/settings/api-keys). 2. Open the Admin UI URL from the server log. 3. Open NVIDIA NIM in **Providers**, click **Add key**, paste the key, and click **Save**. 4. Leave `MODEL` on the default `nvidia_nim/nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b`, or search the model dropdown and select another model. 5. Click **Apply** to save your model selection. To protect the local proxy with a bearer token, enable **Proxy Authentication** in Admin.
### 4. Run Your Coding Agent Claude Code: ```bash fcc-claude ``` Codex: ```bash fcc-codex ``` Pi: ```bash fcc-pi ``` OpenCode 2: ```bash fcc-opencode ``` Cline: ```bash fcc-cline ``` Hermes: ```bash fcc-hermes ``` DeepSeek Harness Web: ```bash fcc-dsh ``` Grok Build: ```bash fcc-grok ``` Muse Code: ```bash fcc-muse ``` Aider: ```bash fcc-aider ``` Antigravity CLI (connect on the Integrations page first): ```bash fcc-agy ``` Other Chat Completions clients can use FCC's server URL followed by `/v1` as their OpenAI-compatible base URL (default `http://127.0.0.1:8082/v1`). Select an FCC model such as `gemini/models/gemini-3.5-flash-lite`. If Proxy Authentication is enabled, use its token as the client's API key. Both streaming and JSON replies are supported.

Select an FCC model from Claude Code's native /model picker.

## Choose A Provider 1. Open a provider link below for its key, models, or setup instructions. 2. In the Admin UI, configure the listed setting. For OpenAI / ChatGPT subscription access, use **Providers → OAuth providers** instead. 3. Search the `MODEL` dropdown and select a model. If the provider cannot list models, enter `/` manually. 4. Click **Apply**. Optional: add an ordered **Fallback Models** list under **Model Config**. It applies to every connected client. A failed request may reach and consume usage from more than one provider before succeeding. Provider modals support numbered API keys. Use **Add key**, remove rows, or drag their handles to reorder them. FCC uses key 1. For another API endpoint, open **Providers → Custom providers → Add provider**. Enter its API base URL, optional keys, and API format. Leave **Model IDs** empty to discover models automatically, or enter one upstream model ID per line. Save, then select a model in **Model Config**.

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling", "hatch-vcs>=0.5.0"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "free-claude-code"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "Local proxy connecting coding agents to OpenAI-compatible AI providers"
readme = "README.md"
license = "AGPL-3.0-only"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
requires-python = "==3.14.10"
dependencies = [
    "packaging>=26.3",
    "anyio>=4.16.0",
    "fastapi[standard]>=0.141.1",
    "uvicorn>=0.54.0",
    "httpx[socks]>=0.28.1",
    "httpx2[socks]>=2.7.0,<3",
    "markdown-it-py>=4.2.0",
    "pydantic>=2.14.3",
    "python-dotenv>=1.2.4",
    "tiktoken>=0.13.0",
    "python-telegram-bot>=22.8",
    "discord.py>=2.7.1",
    "openai>=3.46.0",
    "loguru>=0.7.0",
    "aiohttp>=3.14.5",
    "jsonschema>=4.25.0",
    "json5>=0.17.3",
    "tomlkit>=0.15.2",
    "google-auth[requests]>=2.56.3",
    "requests[socks]>=2.34.2",
    "pystray>=0.19.5; sys_platform == 'win32' or sys_platform == 'darwin'",
    "Pillow>=13.0.0; sys_platform == 'win32' or sys_platform == 'darwin'",
    "github-copilot-sdk>=1.0.29",
    "simplejson>=4.2.0",
    "grpcio>=1.85.1",
    "grpcio-tools>=1.85.1",
    "nvidia-riva-client>=2.28.0",
    "pyperclip>=1.11.0",
    "sqlalchemy>=2.1.8",
    "ruamel-yaml>=0.19.1",
]

[project.scripts]
_fcc-update-check = "free_claude_code.updater.check:main"
fcc-server = "free_claude_code.cli.entrypoints:serve"
fcc-doctor = "free_claude_code.cli.entrypoints:doctor"
fcc-claude = "free_claude_code.cli.launchers.claude:launch"
fcc-codex = "free_claude_code.cli.launchers.codex:launch"
fcc-pi = "free_claude_code.cli.launchers.pi:launch"
fcc-opencode = "free_claude_code.cli.launchers.opencode:launch"
fcc-cline = "free_claude_code.cli.launchers.cline:launch"
fcc-hermes = "free_claude_code.cli.launchers.hermes:launch"
fcc-dsh = "free_claude_code.cli.launchers.dsh:launch"
fcc-grok = "free_claude_code.cli.launchers.grok:launch"
fcc-muse = "free_claude_code.cli.launchers.muse:launch"
fcc-agy = "free_claude_code.cli.launchers.agy:launch"
fcc-aider = "free_claude_code.cli.launchers.aider:launch"

[project.gui-scripts]
fcc-desktop = "free_claude_code.cli.desktop_entrypoint:launch"

[project.optional-dependencies]
voice_local = [
    "torch>=2.14.1",
    "transformers>=5.22.2",
    "accelerate>=1.15.0",
    "librosa>=1.0.0",
]

[tool.hatch.version]
source = "vcs"

[tool.hatch.build]
artifacts = ["src/free_claude_code/assets/macos/fcc-desktop-*"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/free_claude_code"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.shared-scripts]
"scripts/update/fcc-update" = "fcc-update"
"scripts/update/fcc-update.cmd" = "fcc-update.cmd"

[tool.uv]
required-version = ">=0.13.7"
cache-keys = [{ file = "pyproject.toml" }, { git = { commit = true, tags = true } }]

[tool.uv.sources]
torch = { index = "pytorch-cu130" }

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pytorch-cu130"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130"
explicit = true

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=9.2.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=1.4.1.post1",
    "pytest-cov>=7.1.0",
    "ty>=0.0.99",
    "ruff>=0.17.4",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.8.0",
    "pytest-playwright>=0.10.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.3",
    "pytest-split>=0.11.0",
    "google-genai>=3.0.0",
]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py314"
line-length = 88

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",    # pycodestyle errors
    "W",    # pycodestyle warnings
    "F",    # Pyflakes (undefined names, unused imports)
    "I",    # isort (import ordering)
    "UP",   # pyupgrade (modernise syntax for target Python version)
    "B",    # flake8-bugbear (common bugs and anti-patterns)
    "C4",   # flake8-comprehensions (idiomatic comprehensions)
    "SIM",  # flake8-simplify (simplifiable code patterns)
    "PERF", # Perflint (performance anti-patterns)
    "RUF",  # Ruff-specific rules
]
ignore = [
    "E501",  # line too long — enforced by the formatter instead
    "B008",  # FastAPI Depends() in argument defaults is intentional
    "RUF006",  # fire-and-forget tasks intentionally not awaited
]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["free_claude_code", "smoke"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"
indent-style = "space"
line-ending = "auto"
skip-magic-trailing-comma = false

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["src", "."]
addopts = "-p e2e.thread_diagnostics -n auto --dist=worksteal"
tmp_path_retention_policy = "failed"
asyncio_default_fixture_loop_scope = "function"
filterwarnings = [
    "error",
    # Starlette's test client uses this deprecated alias, including in 1.6.0.
    'ignore:^The anyio\.abc\.BlockingPortal alias is deprecated, use anyio\.from_thread\.BlockingPortal instead\.$:DeprecationWarning:^starlette\.testclient$',
    # pytest 9.2 deprecates pytest-playwright 0.10.0's plugin-class base_url fixture.
    'ignore:^Session-scoped fixtures defined as instance methods are deprecated\.\nInstance attributes set in the .base_url. fixture:pytest.PytestRemovedIn10Warning:^_pytest\.fixtures$',
]
testpaths = ["tests"]
markers = [
    "live

readme_content:
# OpenBot ### AI coworkers. Ready for the enterprise. A modular, self-hostable workspace for AI coworkers.
Choose your models. Bring your agents. Own your infrastructure. [open.bot](https://open.bot) · [Docs](docs/README.md) · [Deploy on Kubernetes](#deploy-on-kubernetes) · [Run from source](#run-from-source) [![GitHub Trending: #3 Repository Of The Day](https://trendshift.io/api/badge/repositories/175080)](https://trendshift.io/repositories/175080) [![Trendshift: #3 Repository Of The Day](https://trendshift.io/api/badge/trendshift/repositories/175080/daily)](https://trendshift.io/repositories/175080)
[![Download for Mac (Apple silicon)](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/CopilotKit/OpenBot?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=3A3466&logo=data%3Aimage%2Fsvg%2Bxml%3Bbase64%2CPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCAyNCAyNCI%2BPHBhdGggZmlsbD0iI2ZmZiIgZD0iTTExIDNoMnYxMC4ybDMuNi0zLjZMMTggMTFsLTYgNi02LTYgMS40LTEuNCAzLjYgMy42ek01IDE5aDE0djJINXoiLz48L3N2Zz4%3D&label=Download%20for%20Mac%20%28Apple%20silicon%29&color=6E6AE0)](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-arm64.dmg) [![Download for Mac (Intel)](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/CopilotKit/OpenBot?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=3A3466&logo=data%3Aimage%2Fsvg%2Bxml%3Bbase64%2CPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCAyNCAyNCI%2BPHBhdGggZmlsbD0iI2ZmZiIgZD0iTTExIDNoMnYxMC4ybDMuNi0zLjZMMTggMTFsLTYgNi02LTYgMS40LTEuNCAzLjYgMy42ek01IDE5aDE0djJINXoiLz48L3N2Zz4%3D&label=Download%20for%20Mac%20%28Intel%29&color=4A7CC8)](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-x64.dmg) [![Download for Windows](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/CopilotKit/OpenBot?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=3A3466&logo=data%3Aimage%2Fsvg%2Bxml%3Bbase64%2CPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZpZXdCb3g9IjAgMCAyNCAyNCI%2BPHBhdGggZmlsbD0iI2ZmZiIgZD0iTTExIDNoMnYxMC4ybDMuNi0zLjZMMTggMTFsLTYgNi02LTYgMS40LTEuNCAzLjYgMy42ek01IDE5aDE0djJINXoiLz48L3N2Zz4%3D&label=Download%20for%20Windows&color=9A5CC6)](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-windows-x64-setup.exe) Notarized .dmg for Apple silicon and Intel Macs · signed installer for Windows x64 · no terminal or developer tools needed · [Release notes](https://github.com/CopilotKit/OpenBot/releases/latest)
[![OpenBot for Business: get early access](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenBot_for_Business-Get_early_access_%E2%86%92-D14B9C?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=3A3466)](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) From [CopilotKit](https://www.copilotkit.ai), creators of [AG-UI](https://github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui).
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c60f07da-8b6d-46eb-a573-17fc1e65a644

Watch a Bot use its browser and tools, answer with interactive results, and wait for your approval before it sends. Take over when it needs you, and connect the agents you already run.

## Getting started ### On your laptop The easiest way to get started is with the fully self-contained app that runs on your laptop, combining the OpenBot frontend and Docker-based backend in one application. [Mac / Apple silicon](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-arm64.dmg) · [Mac / Intel](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-mac-x64.dmg) · [Windows](https://downloads.copilotkit.ai/latest/OpenBot-windows-x64-setup.exe) [Run from source](#run-from-source) ### For your team **OpenBot for Business** brings your agents into one workspace with company sign-in, tool permissions, approvals, and audit. Deploy on your infrastructure or work with our engineers on hosting and customization. [**Get early access to OpenBot for Business →**](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [**Talk to an engineer**](https://open.bot/business) · [**Kubernetes setup**](#deploy-on-kubernetes) ### Web, mobile, and chat [Web](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=web&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [iOS](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=ios&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Android](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=android&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Slack](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=slack&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) · [Teams](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=teams&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access) ## Your workspace. Your stack.
- **Choose your models.** Use OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, or open models through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, hosted by a provider or on your own infrastructure. Keep your provider relationships and change models as your needs change. - **Bring your agents.** Run built-in Bots in the OpenBot server, or connect your existing agents through AG-UI from any agent execution platform. Agents built with different stacks can work in the same workspace. - **Make it yours.** Use the MIT-licensed template as-is, white-label it, or customize it deeply. AG-UI connects agents, MCP connects tools, and the frontends and backend can evolve independently. - **Govern work across your team.** Company sign-in, roles, tool permissions, approvals, and audit apply across the workspace. Your agents use OpenBot's tools and computers under the same policies. - **Get help deploying it.** CopilotKit's engineers can work with your team to deploy OpenBot, connect your systems, and automate parts of specific jobs. [Connect your agent](#bring-your-own-agent) · [Configure models and tools](docs/configuration.md) · [Explore OpenBot for Business](https://open.bot/business) ## Built on CopilotKit and AG-UI OpenBot is built on [CopilotKit](https://www.copilotkit.ai), which is [used in production by a majority of Fortune 500 companies](https://www.copilotkit.ai/blog/series-a). **Your agent stack.** [AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com/introduction#supported-integrations) has first-class integrations across the major agent frameworks and harnesses, including Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK, Microsoft Agent Framework and Agent Harness, Google ADK, AWS Strands, Oracle Agent Spec, LangChain, Mastra, Pydantic AI, Agno, and CrewAI. Many ship first-party support; [Amazon Bedrock AgentCore supports AG-UI directly](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-agui.html). **Your execution platform.** Keep your agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Claude Managed Agents, [Google's Agent Platform](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform), LangChain's Managed Deep Agents, [Microsoft Foundry Agent Service](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agents), or your own infrastructure. Connect them to OpenBot through an AG-UI endpoint, using an adapter where needed. Your choice of agent platform stays independent of your workspace. ## Architecture OpenBot has three parts. On your laptop, setup runs the backend and Intelligence for you. For a team, the Helm chart deploys both on Kubernetes in your own infrastructure. | Part | What it does | | --- | --- | | **OpenBot frontends** | Mac, Windows, web, iOS, Android, Slack, and Teams connect people to the same workspace. Conversations, interactive results, computer view, and approvals adapt to each surface. [Choose a frontend](#getting-started). | | **OpenBot backend** | Runs the workspace API and built-in Bots, connects external agents and tools, manages Bot computers, and enforces identity, permissions, action policies, and audit. Deploys on Kubernetes with PostgreSQL and persistent storage. | | **CopilotKit Intelligence** | Durable conversations, memory, Automatic Learning, and enterprise governance services. Separately licensed; runs on Kubernetes alongside OpenBot. | OpenBot enforces sign-in, tool permissions, action policies, and audit at its API, alongside Intelligence's platform services. Built-in Bots run in the OpenBot server; your own agents can run alongside OpenBot or on any agent execution platform. Both use AG-UI and can share the same workspace. Computer execution is pluggable: use the default Kubernetes setup or connect a compatible external computer provider. [Architecture details](docs/architecture.md) · [Services and ports](#services-and-ports) · [Kubernetes deployment](#deploy-on-kubernetes) ## Open source, local operation, and licensing **The OpenBot application template is open source under the [MIT license](LICENSE).** You can fork, modify, and white-label it. It uses **CopilotKit Intelligence**, which is separately licensed and can run entirely on your own machine or infrastructure. | Where you run it | CopilotKit Intelligence license | | --- | --- | | **Your laptop, for personal use and experimentation** | Requires a free local Intelligence license. Desktop setup handles this for you. | | **Kubernetes evaluation** | Requires a free Intelligence trial license. [Request a trial](https://dashboard.operations.copilotkit.ai/early-access/openbot?platform=business&ref=github&utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=openbot-early-access). | | **Kubernetes / production** | Requires a production Intelligence license beyond evaluation. OpenBot for Business includes Intelligence for use with OpenBot. [Plans and pricing](https://open.bot/pricing). | **Fully local is an option.** Run OpenBot, Intelligence, and a compatible model locally. A cloud model or connected online app still sends requests to that service. Initial downloads, account sign-in, and local license renewal need internet access. --- ## Deploy on Kubernetes Deploy OpenBot and CopilotKit Intelligence together on **AWS EKS, Azure AKS, Google GKE, or your own Kubernetes cluster**. The chart installs Intelligence by default; no separate hosted project is required. For a first evaluation, you need a cluster with **amd64 nodes**, a **default StorageClass**, `kubectl`, Helm, a **trial or production license**, and a model key. The commands below use an OpenAI key. name: taste-skill
description: Agent skills that give coding agents taste: art direction, reference images and a browser check instead of generic AI pages
readme_content:
Sponsors

interfaces.dev · A design engineering magazine by Jakub Krehel
React Bits · animated React components for creative interfaces
IMG.LY · CreativeEditor SDK
Sent.dm · messaging APIs for SMS, WhatsApp, and RCS

Become a sponsor

**Taste Skill** (`tasteskill 2.5.1`) is an Agent Skill that makes coding agents build professional company websites at the `figma.com` and `x.ai` level instead of assembling a generic landing page. Every build uses plain copy, one design system, one section per screen, equal left and right edges, real photographs (licensed stand-ins when the client has none), real brand icons and real product UI, a hero entrance and one or two dealt moments on every page, quiet micro-interactions, and shader effects and scroll scenes kept strictly for tech, gaming and software pages, all verified in a real browser by a checker and a finish gate that enforce the rules. Pages built from a single brief in earlier v2 runs:
The photographs are real, found in open archives and credited by the skill ([credits](examples/v2/CREDITS.md)). Watch the [launch film](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill/releases/tag/v2.0.0). ## Install ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill --skill "design-taste-frontend" ``` That installs the skill with the [`npx skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills) CLI. The skill runs its scripts with **Node 22+** and an installed **Chrome, Edge or Chromium** (set `CHROME_PATH` if it is in a non-standard place). Optional: **ffmpeg** on the PATH, for WebP output and the phone crop of a hero photograph in `photos.mjs`. It installs nothing and needs no API keys. Bundled Wikimedia Commons photographs work offline; fetching additional photographs or icons uses network access.
Claude Code plugin Run these inside Claude Code. The skill is namespaced under `taste-skill:`, so it does not collide with your other skills. ``` /plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill /plugin install taste-skill@taste-skill ``` `/plugin update` upgrades it later.
Codex plugin ```bash codex plugin marketplace add Leonxlnx/taste-skill codex plugin add taste-skill@taste-skill ``` Start a new Codex session afterwards so the skill is loaded.
From a clone, linked instead of copied `./install.sh` symlinks the skill into Claude Code (`--codex` for Codex, `--all-agents` for both), so a `git pull` updates it in place. On Windows (Git Bash) it makes a real link, or a directory junction when symlinks are not allowed, and it reports an older copied folder instead of skipping it silently.
Already have the skill? Run the install command again; the install name did not change. Looking for one of the older skills? See [Moved skills](#moved-skills). ## How 2.5 works Use it by asking your agent to build or redesign a company site; the agent loads the skill, copies `assets/` into the project, starts from `assets/starter.html` and runs the checker before it hands the page over. Every build starts by classifying the client's business (`software`, `gaming`, `tech`, `product`, `service` or `place`) and planning the page screen by screen before writing markup: 1. **Deal tokens and layout.** `scripts/start.mjs` deals a palette made for the trade and a Google Fonts pairing for the page kind (`library/palettes.json`, `library/type.json`), and `assets/layout/deal.mjs` deals a hero layout (`split`, `centred`, `product`, `photo`, `place`, `collage`, `editorial`, `word`, `film`, `statement` or `triptych`). 2. **Start from one system.** `assets/starter.html`, `assets/system.css` and `assets/layout/layout.css` enforce one section per screen at desktop (`1440x900`), equal left and right content edges, a fixed navigation bar and a single-screen closing footer (`footer.closing`). 3. **Show real product UI and real photographs.** Software and tech pages populate lit feature cards (`assets/ui/cards.css`) with rewritten HTML UI fragments (`assets/ui/`) and node-and-line diagrams (`assets/diagrams/`), with real brand and interface SVGs resolved locally by `scripts/icons.mjs`. Place, shop, hospitality and non-technical product pages lead with curated photographs (`scripts/photos.mjs`, `assets/photos/`), typography and flat colour, crediting sources in one expandable footer line with no captions under images. 4. **Keep effects for tech and gaming pages.** Shader grounds (`scripts/effects.mjs`), scroll scenes (`assets/scenes/`) and procedural 3D prints (`assets/objects/`) are dealt only on `software`, `tech` and `gaming` pages within a four-context WebGL cap, with static fallbacks for phones and reduced motion. Every page gets a hero entrance and one or two moments from `scripts/moments.mjs`; cafes, hotels, shops, studios and services get only the photo- and type-led ones, and zero WebGL. 5. **Check in a real browser over HTTP.** `scripts/consistency.mjs`, `assets/layout/check.mjs`, `scripts/perf.mjs` and `scripts/shoot.mjs` render the built page in headless Chrome across `1440`, `1024`, `768` and `390`, catching empty visuals, broken shaders, contrast drops, misaligned columns, section-height drift, placeholder text, invented street numbers and slow-network image gaps before the build ships. `scripts/gate.mjs` then holds the finish until no fixable FAIL is left, three rounds at most. Details of what changed from `2.1.x` are in the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md). ## The tools Everything is a plain Node 22+ script in the skill folder; none installs anything. | Tool | What it does | | --- | --- | | `scripts/start.mjs` | Deals a palette and a Google Fonts pairing for the page kind and prints the `` links and `:root` tokens. | | `assets/layout/deal.mjs` | Deals one of eleven tested hero layouts; `assets/layout/check.mjs` checks it with long-headline stress tests. | | `scripts/photos.mjs` | Deals vetted photographs by trade, enforces image weight and writes the one footer credit line. | | `scripts/icons.mjs` | Resolves real brand and interface icons into local SVG files. | | `scripts/effects.mjs`, `scripts/moments.mjs` | Deal shader grounds for tech, gaming and software pages, and the moments for every kind. | | `scripts/gate.mjs`, `scripts/copy-lint.mjs` | The finish gate (also a Stop hook) and the copy linter it runs. | | `scripts/consistency.mjs` | The checker: renders the page in headless Chrome over HTTP at `1440`, `1024`, `820`, `768` and `390` and prints PASS, WARN or FAIL per rule. | | `scripts/perf.mjs`, `scripts/shoot.mjs` | Page weight and speed, and full-page and per-section screenshots. | First run, from the project folder (a deal also arms the finish gate there): `node scripts/start.mjs deal --page software` (kinds: `software`, `gaming`, `tech`, `product`, `service`, `place`). Check a built page with `node scripts/consistency.mjs --page `. ## Moved skills This repo holds one skill, `design-taste-frontend`. The others moved to repos of their own and kept their install names: | Install name | Where it lives now | | --- | --- | | `high-end-visual-design`, `minimalist-ui`, `industrial-brutalist-ui`, `gpt-taste`, `stitch-design-taste`, `design-taste-frontend-v1`, `design-taste-frontend-v2-experimental` | **[Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics)** | | `imagegen-frontend-web`, `imagegen-frontend-mobile`, `brandkit`, `image-to-code` | **[Leonxlnx/imagegen-skills](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/imagegen-skills)** | | `redesign-existing-projects` | Part of `design-taste-frontend`, which audits an existing page in a real browser before changing anything | | `full-output-enforcement` | Removed. For the same problem, see **[Leonxlnx/unlazy](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/unlazy)** | Install a moved skill from its new repo under the same name: ```bash npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill-classics --skill "high-end-visual-design" ``` ## Common Questions **What does the skill need?** Node 22 or newer and Chrome, Edge or Chromium; ffmpeg is optional (WebP photographs and the phone crop of a hero photograph). It installs nothing and uses no API keys. Bundled Commons photographs are stored locally; network access is used only when downloading additional photographs, Google Fonts or brand icons. **Where do the pictures come from, and can I use them?** From the skill's vetted photograph library (`assets/photos/photos.json`, including bundled Wikimedia Commons WebP sets and Unsplash photographs) dealt by `scripts/photos.mjs`. name: codex-security
description: OpenAI's Codex Security CLI and TypeScript SDK for finding, validating, and fixing security vulnerabilities. npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openai/codex-security
readme_content:
# Codex Security

Codex Security helps you find, investigate, and fix vulnerabilities in your code.
Use its security workflows in Codex, or automate them with the
`@openai/codex-security` CLI and TypeScript SDK.

- **In Codex:** [choose a security workflow](docs/agent-workflows.md).
- **In a terminal:** [install the CLI and scan your repository](#quick-start).
- **In automation:** use the [TypeScript SDK](#typescript-sdk) or
  [GitHub Action](#github-actions).

## Features

- Scan repositories, selected paths, or Git changes. Deep scans repeat Standard scans and return their deduplicated findings.
- Validate candidate findings, generate patches, and verify existing fixes.
- Draft `SECURITY.md` policies and save threat models for later review.
- Browse saved scans and findings, identify duplicates, assess severity against
  your own rubric, and suggest owners from source and Git history.
- Preview third-party scanner findings, save them locally, or publish supported reports to Codex Security Cloud. [Scanner import guides](docs/scanner-imports/README.md).
- Track findings in Linear, Jira, or GitHub, publish completed scans, or export SARIF, JSON, and CSV. [Integration workflows](docs/plugin-connectors.md).
- Automate scans across repositories or project components, including in CI and
  containers.

## Use in Codex

Open your repository in a Codex session with the Codex Security plugin enabled,
then ask:

> Run a Codex Security scan on this repository, focusing on authentication and
> authorization. Return the saved report, source evidence, and coverage limits.

A completed scan saves a report and findings. Read the report for source
evidence and exclusions, then request a patch or ask Codex to verify an
existing fix. See the [agent workflow guide](docs/agent-workflows.md) for setup,
task selection, and recovery.

## Quick start

Requires Node.js 22.13.0+ within 22.x, or Node.js 24.x or 26.x, and Python 3.10+.
Python 3.10 also requires `tomli`.

Install the CLI globally and sign in:

```bash
npm install --global @openai/codex-security
cs login
```

Run your first scan from the repository directory:

```bash
cs scan .
```

When the scan completes, open the Markdown file at the **REPORT** path in the
terminal. Run `cs scans show` from the same repository to find its latest
completed scan again. See [scan scope and follow-up work](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#understand-scan-scope-and-follow-up-work)
for how to interpret exclusions in the report.

`cs` and `codex-security` run the same CLI. If the short name conflicts with
another command, use `codex-security`. To skip the global install, or if npm
reports an `EEXIST` conflict, use `npx @openai/codex-security` in place of
`cs` for both login and scanning.

For CI, set `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `CODEX_API_KEY` in the scan process's environment.
For a headless machine, see [device or SSH login](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#authentication).

### Scan options

Choose a scope and scan mode:

```bash
# Scan selected paths.
cs scan . --path src --path tests

# Scan committed changes from a base revision to HEAD.
cs scan . --diff origin/main

# Run a deep scan of the repository.
cs scan . --mode deep
```

Use `cs scan . --max-time 15` for an advisory 15-minute Standard investigation
allowance. See [investigation time](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#set-investigation-time)
for timing semantics and Deep Scan limits.

Use `cs --help` to browse commands, or `cs scan --help`
for scan options, cost limits, and patching after a scan.

For an application spread across repositories, see
[review one system across repositories](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#review-one-system-across-repositories).
Use [bulk scans](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#bulk-scans) for independent repository
reviews in one resumable campaign.

Scans use existing root and component `SECURITY.md` guidance. To write or
revise it, see [Generate SECURITY.md](#generate-securitymd).

Some cybersecurity requests and protected findings require
[Trusted Access for Cyber](https://chatgpt.com/cyber). For accounts with Daybreak
access, see [Daybreak opt-in](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#daybreak-opt-in) for the
Codex toggle and [Cyber access programs](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#select-a-cyber-access-program)
to select a program explicitly.

## TypeScript SDK

Install the package locally in your TypeScript project:

```bash
npm install @openai/codex-security
```

Then import it:

```ts
import { CodexSecurity } from "@openai/codex-security";

const security = new CodexSecurity();

try {
  const result = await security.run("/path/to/repository");
  console.log(result.reportPath);
} finally {
  await security.close();
}
```

The [SDK guide](sdk/typescript/docs/sdk.md) includes deep-scan configuration,
validation, severity classification, owner suggestions, and result handling.

Linked Git worktrees share scan history and saved findings when they use the same
Codex Security state directory. Keep `CODEX_SECURITY_STATE_DIR` stable to retain
that shared history and sign-in scope. See the [scan history guide](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#scan-history-and-reruns).

## Read existing Cloud findings

When Codex Security Cloud is available to your account, the Security plugin's
`$cloud-findings` skill can read findings, reports, recorded assignment and
verification, and scan status in Codex desktop or the Codex CLI. Cloud is an
optional connection; local scans work without it.

See [Cloud connection setup and CLI reads](sdk/typescript/docs/sdk.md#read-existing-cloud-findings)
for authentication requirements and a read-only example.

## Generate SECURITY.md

Use `policy` to draft a new `SECURITY.md` or update an existing one. Use `--path`
to select a component:

```bash
cs policy .
cs policy . --path services/api --knowledge-base architecture.md
```

The command saves its draft outside the repository and leaves existing files
unchanged. Review the diff and notes, edit the draft, then copy only `SECURITY.md`
to the displayed **Policy target**. Keep the saved architecture and threat-model
documents outside the repository.

Scans already use root and component `SECURITY.md` files. Keep your current policy
if it needs no changes. When updating it, preserve its vulnerability-reporting
instructions. If the command says the policy is already up to date, no copy is
needed.

Files at `.github/SECURITY.md` or `docs/SECURITY.md` often contain reporting
instructions. Preserve them when drafting a policy; those locations do not
automatically provide repository-wide scan guidance. See the
[policy guide](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#generate-a-security-policy) for policy
locations, unanswered questions, saved artifacts, and SDK usage.

## Save and export threat models

Scans and policy generation save threat models with their results. Export a saved
model without starting another analysis:

```bash
cs export --scan SCAN_ID --artifact threat-model --output threatmodel.md
```

Omit `--scan` to use the current repository's latest completed scan. The
[export guide](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#exports-and-ci) also covers findings,
SARIF output for CI, and the offline TypeScript API. For ServiceNow Application
Vulnerability Response, see [Export findings for ServiceNow](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#export-findings-for-servicenow).

## GitHub Actions

To run a weekly repository scan on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu:

1. Add an OpenAI API key as the repository secret `CODEX_SECURITY_API_KEY`.
2. Copy the [weekly workflow](github-action/examples/repository.yml) to
   `.github/workflows/codex-security.yml`. Replace `REPLACE_WITH_REVIEWED_COMMIT`
   with the reviewed distribution commit SHA from an Action release.
3. To try the workflow before the next scheduled run, open **Actions → Codex
   Security repository → Run workflow**.

The example uses an estimated $5 limit per scan and reports findings without
failing the job. Requests in progress can exceed the limit. For a severity
threshold, pull request checks, or runner requirements, see the
[Action guide](github-action/README.md). For eligible accounts, see
[Daybreak access](github-action/README.md#daybreak-access-and-refusals).

## Containerized bulk scans

Scan a list of repositories with the included Docker Compose configuration,
which keeps results and authentication between runs. See the
[container quick start](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#containerized-bulk-scans).
The [workflow runner](docker/README.md#workflow-runner) runs individual CLI stages
in containers and can connect to a separately deployed findings service.

## Findings storage and deduplication

The [findings guide](sdk/typescript/docs/findings-service.md) covers local
storage, deduplication, and compatibility with independently operated endpoints
through `publish scan --to custom` and explicit `--findings-url`. The local
`serve` command and browser dashboard have been removed; existing databases and
scan artifacts remain available.

## Other providers

Scans support OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, OpenRouter, Fireworks AI, and Cheaper Inference. Bedrock uses
AWS credentials and does not require a separate OpenAI login. See
[Bedrock setup](docs/bedrock.md) for AWS profiles, regions, and model access.

For OpenRouter, Fireworks AI, and Cheaper Inference, set the provider's API key and choose a supported
model. See [provider configuration](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md#native-command-authentication-and-other-providers)
for examples.

## Documentation

- [Online documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/security/cli)
- [Agent workflows and recovery](docs/agent-workflows.md)
- [CLI reference](sdk/typescript/docs/cli.md)
- [Imported finding identity and evidence](docs/scanner-imports/schema-guide.md)
- [Project configuration](docs/project-configuration.md)
- [Examples](examples/README.md)

To report a vulnerability privately, follow the [security policy](SECURITY.md).

name: agent-skills
description: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.
readme_content:
# Agent Skills **Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.** Skills encode the workflows, quality gates, and best practices that senior engineers use when building software. These ones are packaged so AI agents follow them consistently across every phase of development. ![Addy's Agent Skills](https://addyosmani.com/assets/images/addys-agent-skills.jpg) ``` DEFINE PLAN BUILD VERIFY REVIEW SHIP ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ ┌──────┐ │ Idea │ ───▶ │ Spec │ ───▶ │ Code │ ───▶ │ Test │ ───▶ │ QA │ ───▶ │ Go │ │Refine│ │ PRD │ │ Impl │ │Debug │ │ Gate │ │ Live │ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ └──────┘ /spec /plan /build /test /review /ship ``` --- ## Commands 9 slash commands that map to the development lifecycle. Each one activates the right skills automatically. | What you're doing | Command | Key principle | |-------------------|---------|---------------| | Define what to build | `/spec` | Spec before code | | Plan how to build it | `/plan` | Small, atomic tasks | | Build incrementally | `/build` | One slice at a time | | Prove it works | `/test` | Tests are proof | | Set the quality bar | `/constraints` | Decide it once, enforce it everywhere | | Review before merge | `/review` | Improve code health | | Audit web performance | `/webperf` | Measure before you optimize | | Simplify the code | `/code-simplify` | Clarity over cleverness | | Ship to production | `/ship` | Faster is safer | In Claude Code these install as plugin commands. Where a built-in command has the same name, as `/review` does, use the namespaced form: `/agent-skills:review`. Want fewer manual steps once the spec exists? **`/build auto`** generates the plan and implements every task in a single approved pass — you approve the plan once, then it runs autonomously. It removes the human stepping *between* tasks, not the verification: every task is still test-driven and committed individually, and it pauses on failures or risky steps. Skills also activate automatically based on what you're doing — designing an API triggers `api-and-interface-design`, building UI triggers `frontend-ui-engineering`, and so on. --- ## Quick Start **Fastest path — any agent, one command.** The open [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) installs into 70+ agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot, Cline, and more): ```bash npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills # install all 25 skills npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --list # browse before installing ``` Or grab individual skills: ```bash npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill code-review-and-quality # five-axis review before merge npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill interview-me # requirements interrogation, one question at a time npx skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --skill test-driven-development # red-green-refactor, enforced ``` > **Installing one skill?** A per-skill `npx` install copies only > `skills//`, not the repo-level `references/` directory. The skill still > works, but paths to supplementary shared checklists are unavailable. Use a > whole-repo integration, clone the repository, or copy the needed checklist into > a `references/` directory inside the installed skill. This portability gap is > tracked in [#361](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills/issues/361). Prefer a native integration? Pick your tool below.
Claude Code (recommended) **Marketplace install:** ``` /plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills /plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills ``` > **SSH errors?** The marketplace clones repos via SSH. If you don't have SSH keys set up on GitHub, either [add your SSH key](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/connecting-to-github-with-ssh/adding-a-new-ssh-key-to-your-github-account) or use the full HTTPS URL to force HTTPS cloning during the marketplace-add step: > ```bash > /plugin marketplace add https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git > /plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills > ``` > > If `/plugin install` still fails with `git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey)` on Windows or macOS, the recommended workaround is to configure Git once to rewrite GitHub SSH URLs to HTTPS for subprocess clones: > ```bash > git config --global url."https://github.com/".insteadOf git@github.com: > ``` **Local / development:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git claude --plugin-dir /path/to/agent-skills ```
Cursor Put workflow skills under `.cursor/skills/` (sync from `agent-skills/skills/`) and short policies in `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` — do not paste full skills into rules. Both directories live in your project; this repo does not ship a `.cursor/` folder. See [docs/cursor-setup.md](docs/cursor-setup.md).
Antigravity CLI Install as a native plugin for skills and subagents. In affected Antigravity CLI releases, legacy command TOMLs are reported as converted but their wrapper commands are not discoverable; invoke the underlying namespaced skills directly. See [docs/antigravity-setup.md](docs/antigravity-setup.md#lifecycle-workflows-and-command-compatibility). **Install from the repo:** ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git ``` **Install from a local clone:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git agy plugin install ./agent-skills ```
Gemini CLI Install as native skills for auto-discovery, or add to `GEMINI.md` for persistent context. See [docs/gemini-cli-setup.md](docs/gemini-cli-setup.md). **Install from the repo:** ```bash gemini skills install https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills.git --path skills ``` **Install from a local clone:** ```bash gemini skills install ./agent-skills/skills/ ```
Windsurf Add skill contents to your Windsurf rules configuration. See [docs/windsurf-setup.md](docs/windsurf-setup.md).
OpenCode Copy skills to `.opencode/skills/` (or `~/.config/opencode/skills/`), add a project-local `AGENTS.md`, and use the built-in `skill` tool for agent-driven execution. Optional slash commands can be added under `.opencode/commands/`. See [docs/opencode-setup.md](docs/opencode-setup.md).
GitHub Copilot Use agent definitions from `agents/` as Copilot personas and skill content in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. The lifecycle slash commands (`/spec`, `/plan`, `/build`, `/test`, `/review`, `/ship`) are Claude Code commands and do not appear in Copilot; invoke the skills by name (`/spec-driven-development`, …) instead. See [docs/copilot-setup.md](docs/copilot-setup.md). Using the standalone `copilot` CLI? Install it as a plugin — see [docs/copilot-cli-setup.md](docs/copilot-cli-setup.md).
Kiro IDE & CLI Skills for Kiro reside under ".kiro/skills/" and can be stored under Project or Global level. Kiro also supports Agents.md. See Kiro docs at https://kiro.dev/docs/skills/
Codex Install as a native Codex plugin (Codex CLI v0.122+): ```bash codex plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills codex plugin add agent-skills@agent-skills ``` The first command registers the marketplace; the second installs the plugin. Codex reads the root `skills/` directory directly through `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`. Once installed, invoke skills in chat using `@` (e.g., `@spec-driven-development`). See [docs/codex-setup.md](docs/codex-setup.md) for local installation and troubleshooting.
Command Code Install natively with the built-in `cmd skills` command. Command Code clones the repo, discovers every `SKILL.md`, and installs into `.commandcode/skills/`: ```bash cmd skills add addyosmani/agent-skills # pick skills to install (project) cmd skills add addyosmani/agent-skills --global # install for all projects (~/.commandcode/skills/) cmd skills add addyosmani/agent-skills -s spec-driven-development # install a specific skill ``` Installed skills show up in the TUI slash menu, e.g. `/spec-driven-development`. See [docs/commandcode-setup.md](docs/commandcode-setup.md).
Other Agents Skills are plain Markdown - they work with any agent that accepts system prompts or instruction files. See [docs/getting-started.md](docs/getting-started.md). Hosts that install the pack but aren't listed above are in [docs/other-hosts.md](docs/other-hosts.md).
--- ## Adoption Already installed? How you roll the pack out depends on your codebase. The **[Adoption Guide](docs/adoption-guide.md)** covers two paths: the full lifecycle from day one for a greenfield project, or an incremental, verification-first rollout for an established codebase. --- ## All 25 Skills The commands above are entry points. The pack includes 25 skills total — 24 lifecycle skills plus the `using-agent-skills` meta-skill. Each skill is a structured workflow with steps, verification gates, and anti-rationalization tables. You can also reference any skill directly. ### Meta - Discover which skill applies | Skill | What It Does | Use When | |-------|-------------|----------| | [using-agent-skills](skills/using-agent-skills/SKILL.md) | Maps incoming work to the right skill workflow and defines shared operating rules | Starting a session or deciding which skill applies | ### Define - name: ponytail
description: Makes your AI agent think like the laziest senior dev in the room. The best code is the code you never wrote.
readme_content:
Ponytail

He says nothing. He writes one line. It works.

Ponytail 5: rebuilt from the ground up.
-53% code · -41% time · -26% cost · -45% tokens
And yet: 98% of risky logic ships with a test. Without Ponytail: 68%.
Benchmarked in Claude Code, the same agent with and without the skill: 39 tasks including a real FastAPI + React repo, Opus 5.5, 5 runs each. Details.

Español · 한국어 · 简体中文 · 日本語

---

## Already built with Ponytail --- You know him. Long ponytail. Oval glasses. Has been at the company longer than the version control. You show him fifty lines; he looks at them, says nothing, and replaces them with one. Ponytail puts him inside your AI agent. ## Numbers

Two things the chart does not show: in a blind comparison, Ponytail 5's replies beat the previous Ponytail's 110 to 67. And on the six security tasks (SQL injection, path traversal, forged tokens, rate limiting, malformed CSV rows, caching) it passed all 30 runs: less code, no less safe. Method, per-task tables and limits: [benchmarks/results/2026-10-07-agentic.md](benchmarks/results/2026-10-07-agentic.md). **The rule was never "fewest tokens."** It is: write only what the task needs, and never cut validation, error handling, security, or accessibility. The code ends up small because it is necessary, not golfed. Lower cost and latency are a side effect. ## Before / after

You ask for a date picker. Without Ponytail, the agent installs a date picker library or builds a whole calendar by hand: 335 lines. Ponytail 5 first looks at what is already there: the repo has an `Input` component, and every browser has a date picker. It puts the two together. 10 lines. More survivors in [examples/](examples/). ## The review, rebuilt

`/ponytail-review` used to look only for code to cut. Now it reviews like the senior dev who gets paged when it breaks: it reads the code your change touches, not just the diff, and checks bugs, security, real load, missing tests, speed, and what to cut. Each finding says what the code does, what goes wrong, how to fix it, and what happens if you don't. ## The audit, rebuilt

`/ponytail-audit` runs the same checks on the whole repo. It maps the code first: entry points, how data moves, what load the project expects. Then it ranks what it finds and tells you what to fix first. The old audit only listed what to delete. ## New in 5.3: the band

In Claude Code, ponytail now shows a band above the prompt: what the current task costs, how many tokens and how much agent time it used, how often it reused existing code instead of writing new code, and whether the tests passed after the last change. Its buttons switch the level, run `/ponytail-review` or `/ponytail-audit`, copy the task as Markdown, and fold the band into one line. Don't want it? `/ponytail band` hides it, the same command brings it back. Needs Claude Code 2.1.290 or later, in the terminal or the desktop app. It does not show in the VS Code chat panel, cloud sessions or `claude -p`.

**Board** opens a local page with every task across your projects: cost, agent time and tokens over time, every session with its tests, and the days you worked. By default, everything stays on your machine, in `~/.config/ponytail/band/`. `/ponytail band import` adds your past Claude Code sessions to it, with their cost, agent time and tokens. ## How it works

The ladder runs *after* it understands the problem, not instead of it: it reads the code the change touches and traces the real flow before picking a rung. Lazy about the solution, never about reading. Lazy, not negligent: trust-boundary validation, data-loss handling, security, and accessibility are never on the chopping block. Logic with a branch, a loop, a parser, money or security leaves one small test behind. Every reply ends with what was skipped or not checked and any risk you should know. ## The prompt Ponytail is one prompt: [`skills/ponytail/SKILL.md`](skills/ponytail/SKILL.md). The compact version, for agents that read a rules file, is [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). Everything else in this repo loads that prompt into different agents. ## Install **Claude Code**, as two separate prompts: ``` /plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail ``` ``` /plugin install ponytail@ponytail ``` **Codex:** ```bash codex plugin marketplace add DietrichGebert/ponytail codex plugin add ponytail@ponytail ``` Then open `/hooks` in Codex, trust its two lifecycle hooks, and start a new thread. **Any other agent:** copy [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) into your project, or ask your agent to install [`skills/ponytail/SKILL.md`](skills/ponytail/SKILL.md) as a skill. Step by step for Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini and the rest: **[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)**. That was it. He'd be proud. He won't say it. Active every session, with a handful of commands (see [Commands](#commands)). `/ponytail ultra` exists for when the codebase has wronged you personally. Startup and mode-change text shows the current mode. Only install ponytail from `DietrichGebert/ponytail` on GitHub or `@dietrichgebert/ponytail` on npm. It never ships `.exe` or `.dll` files; a copy that does is not mine. ## Commands | Command | What it does | |---------|--------------| | `/ponytail [lite \| full \| ultra \| off]` | Set the intensity, or turn it off. No argument switches ponytail on at the default level if it is off, and otherwise reports the current level. | | `/ponytail band [on \| off]` | Claude Code only: hide or show the band above the prompt. No argument switches it. The level stays. | | `/ponytail band import` | Claude Code only: add your past Claude Code sessions to the board, with their cost, agent time and tokens. | | `/ponytail-review` | Review the current diff like the senior dev who gets

# ECC Your agent can write code, but ECC gives it a coordinated engineering system and toolbox: it plans before it builds, verifies changes with tests, reviews its own work from a fresh context, remembers what matters, and turns repeated wins into reusable skills and workflows. ```text plan -> test -> implement -> review -> verify -> remember -> improve ``` Instead of rebuilding that process in every prompt, you install it once and make it part of how your agent works. > Optimize the context window. Persist everything else. ECC is MIT-licensed open source. It works best with Claude Code today, has native Codex and Qoder plugin paths, and provides capability-limited adapters for Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, Zed, GitHub Copilot, Antigravity, Qwen, and other harnesses. See the [support status matrix](#platform-support) before assuming feature parity. Access to 71 agents, 314 skills, and 98 legacy command shims, plus hooks, rules, memory, continuous learning, and AgentShield security scanning. readme_content:
[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@qwen-code/qwen-code.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@qwen-code/qwen-code) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/QwenLM/qwen-code.svg)](./LICENSE) [![Node.js Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22.0.0-brightgreen.svg)](https://nodejs.org/) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@qwen-code/qwen-code.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@qwen-code/qwen-code) **The open-source AI coding agent for your terminal, editor, desktop, browser, and chat.** 中文 | Deutsch | français | 日本語 | Русский | Português (Brasil) | 한국어
![Qwen Code in the terminal, desktop app, browser, editor, and chat, with VS Code, Zed, JetBrains, Telegram, DingTalk, WeChat, and Feishu integrations](https://img.alicdn.com/imgextra/i1/O1CN01DXWdF8BDUdD3XPhl_!!6000000001721-2-tps-1743-902.png) | **Qwen Code 1.0 Preview** | | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Qwen Code 1.0 Preview brings together the agent harness capabilities of [Qoder](https://qoder.com/) and Qwen Code in an open-source release.

[Try Qwen Code 1.0 Preview](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/tree/v1.0.0-preview) · [Documentation](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/1.x/) · [中文文档](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/1.x/zh/users/overview/). | ## Why Qwen Code? - **Agentic out of the box** — Auto-Memory, Auto-Skills, SubAgents, Agent Teams, and MCP. Dynamic workflows, zero setup. - **Open-source, inside and out** — The framework and the Qwen models are open-source. They evolve together. No vendor lock-in. - **Multi-protocol** — Supports OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Qwen APIs. Any third-party provider or local model (Ollama / vLLM). Switch at runtime. - **Beyond the terminal** — IDE plugins, Desktop app, Web UI, SDKs, and chat integrations (Telegram / DingTalk / WeChat / Feishu). > [!TIP] > Qwen Code is actively iterating on itself — using its own agent and models to file issues, submit PRs, review code, and run tests. Powered by the community, driven by AI. ## Installation Looking for **Qwen Code 1.0 Preview**? [Get started here](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/tree/v1.0.0-preview). The instructions below are for the main version. **Linux / macOS:** ```bash curl -fsSL https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.sh | bash ``` **Windows:** ```powershell irm https://qwen-code-assets.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/installation/install-qwen-standalone.ps1 | iex ``` > Restart your terminal after installation to ensure environment variables take effect.
NPM / Homebrew **NPM** (requires [Node.js 22+](https://nodejs.org/)): ```bash npm install -g @qwen-code/qwen-code@latest ``` **Homebrew** (macOS / Linux): ```bash brew install qwen-code ```
## Quick Start Open a terminal in your project and start Qwen Code: ```bash cd /path/to/your-project qwen ``` Inside the session, run `/auth` and choose [**Qwen Account with Subscription**](https://chat.qwen.ai/?memberPlan=qwen_code&entry=qwen_code&paywallScene=cli) to sign in with your **Plus or Pro subscription**, or configure a provider with an API key. Then try: ```text Explain this repository and show me where to start. ``` See the [Authentication Guide](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/configuration/auth/) and [Settings Reference](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/configuration/settings/) for detailed setup.
See the terminal interface ![Qwen Code terminal interface](https://img.alicdn.com/imgextra/i2/O1CN01K0nwj41RM1Il8kB0t_!!6000000002096-2-tps-1544-1060.png)
## How to Use Qwen Code Choose the interface that fits your workflow: | Interface | Get started | | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Terminal** | Run `qwen` in your project — see [Quick Start](#quick-start). | | **Desktop** | [Download Qwen Code Desktop](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/releases/tag/desktop-latest) for macOS, Windows, and Linux. | | **Web** | Run `qwen serve --open` to open the [Web UI](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/qwen-serve/) in your browser. _(experimental)_ | | **Editor** | Set up [VS Code](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/integration-vscode/), [Zed](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/integration-zed/), or [JetBrains](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/integration-jetbrains/). | | **Chat** | Connect [Telegram](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/telegram/), [DingTalk](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/dingtalk/), [WeChat](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/weixin/), or [Feishu](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/features/channels/feishu/), then run `qwen channel start`. | For automation and custom integrations: - **Headless** — Run `qwen -p "..."` in scripts, CI/CD, or batch jobs. - **SDKs** — Build with [TypeScript](./packages/sdk-typescript/README.md), [Python](./packages/sdk-python/README.md), or [Java](./packages/sdk-java/qwencode/README.md). - **Daemon** — Run `qwen serve` to connect clients over HTTP + SSE (ACP). _(experimental)_ [Daemon guide](https://qwenlm.github.io/qwen-code-docs/en/users/qwen-serve/). - **Computer Use** — Set up [native MCP tools](./packages/cua-driver/README.md#agent-integration) or [Node REPL + SDK](./packages/node-repl/README.md#usage) in Qwen Code, Claude Code, or Codex.
SDK example (Python) ```python import asyncio from qwen_code_sdk import is_sdk_result_message, query async def main() -> None: result = query( "Summarize the repository layout.", { "cwd": "/path/to/project", "path_to_qwen_executable": "qwen", }, ) async for message in result: if is_sdk_result_message(message): print(message["result"]) asyncio.run(main()) ```
## Daemon Mode Run Qwen Code as a long-lived service when you want browser, editor, SDK, and automation clients to share agent sessions without each starting a separate process. The daemon provides the built-in Web Shell and an HTTP + SSE API, supports multiple workspaces, and lets clients reconnect to active sessions. Start it in the foreground and open the Web Shell: ```bash qwen serve --open ``` The default address is `http://127.0.0.1:4170`. To run and manage it in the background instead: ```bash qwen daemon start qwen daemon status qwen daemon logs -f qwen daemon stop ``` By default, the daemon listens on loopback without bearer authentication; any local process that can reach it can use the full API, including code execution. On shared or untrusted hosts, set `QWEN_SERVER_TOKEN` and use `--require-auth`. See the [Daemon guide](./docs/users/qwen-serve.md) for workspaces, authentication, remote access, and the API. ## Capabilities If you know Claude Code, you already know Qwen Code — and then some. We've put significant effort into [bringing Qwen Code to feature parity with Claude Code](https://github.com/wenshao/codeagents/blob/main/docs/comparison/qwen-code-improvement-report.md), improving both breadth and reliability across the board. | Feature | Qwen Code | Claude Code | | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | :-------: | :---------: | | SubAgents, Agent Teams, Dynamic Workflows | ✓ | ✓ | | Auto-Memory, Auto-Skills, Hooks | ✓ | ✓ | | Built-in Skills (/review, /batch, /loop, /bugfix…) | ✓ | ✓ | | MCP, Plan Mode, LSP Integration | ✓ | ✓ | | Auto Mode, Sandbox, Git Worktrees | ✓ | ✓ | | Computer Use (desktop automation) | ✓ | ✓ | | IDE Plugins (VS Code / JetBrains / Zed) | ✓ | ✓ | | SDK | ✓ | ✓ | | Headless Mode, Session Management | ✓ | ✓ | | Open-source — model and framework | ✓ | — | | Multi-protocol (OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / Qwen + any provider) | ✓ | — | | Agent Arena (multi-model head-to-head on same task) | ✓ | — | | Daemon Mode — `qwen serve` (multi-client shared agent) | ✓ | — | | IM Channels (Telegram / DingTalk / WeChat
