name: claude-plugins-official
description: Official, Anthropic-managed directory of high quality Claude Code Plugins.
readme_content:
# Claude Plugins

Anthropic's own plugins for Claude, and the `claude-plugins-official` marketplace for Claude Code.

> **Submitting a plugin?** Submit it at **[claude.ai/directory/manage](https://claude.ai/directory/manage)**. Plugins accepted there are served across Claude products. Pull requests to this repository are not monitored.

## What is changing

- **All plugins are now submitted at [claude.ai/directory/manage](https://claude.ai/directory/manage)**, and are served across Claude products from there.
- **`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` is being phased out for third-party plugins.** It will be reduced over time to Anthropic's own plugins.
- **This repository is the home of Anthropic's own plugins.** Its checks cover the plugin folders here, not the plugins hosted in other repositories.

> **⚠️ Important:** Make sure you trust a plugin before installing, updating, or using it. Anthropic does not control what MCP servers, files, or other software are included in plugins and cannot verify that they will work as intended or that they won't change. See each plugin's homepage for more information.

## Structure

- **`/plugins`** - Internal plugins developed and maintained by Anthropic
- **`/external_plugins`** - Third-party plugins added before submissions moved to [claude.ai/directory/manage](https://claude.ai/directory/manage), and Anthropic's channel plugins (Discord, fakechat, iMessage and Telegram)

## Installation

Plugins can be installed directly from this marketplace via Claude Code's plugin system.

To install, run `/plugin install {plugin-name}@claude-plugins-official`

or browse for the plugin in `/plugin > Discover`

## Contributing

### Third-party plugins

Submit and manage your plugin at [claude.ai/directory/manage](https://claude.ai/directory/manage). Do not open a pull request here: pull requests are not monitored, and `marketplace.json` is being reduced to Anthropic's own plugins.

### Anthropic plugins

Plugins in `/plugins` are developed by Anthropic team members. See `/plugins/example-plugin` for a reference implementation. Every folder there is checked on each pull request, whether or not `marketplace.json` lists it.

## Plugin Structure

Each plugin follows a standard structure:

```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json      # Plugin metadata (required)
├── .mcp.json            # MCP server configuration (optional)
├── commands/            # Slash commands (optional)
├── agents/              # Agent definitions (optional)
├── skills/              # Skill definitions (optional)
└── README.md            # Documentation
```

## Plugin names are immutable

The `name` field in a marketplace entry is an **immutable slug**. Once a plugin has been published, its `name` must not change — users have it installed under that slug, and renaming it breaks their install with a `plugin-not-found` error.

- To change how a plugin is labeled in the UI, set or update `displayName` instead.
- If a rename is genuinely unavoidable, add an entry to the top-level `renames` map in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` so existing installs auto-migrate:

```json
"renames": {
  "old-name": "new-name"
}
```

The Claude Code plugin loader reads this map and transparently rewrites the old slug to the new one on the user's next sync.

## Skill-bundle plugins

When a plugin's source repository ships skills (`SKILL.md` files) without a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest, the marketplace entry can declare the skills directly using `strict: false` and an explicit `skills` array.

```json
{
  "name": "example-bundle",
  "description": "Brief description of the bundled skills.",
  "author": { "name": "Author Name" },
  "category": "development",
  "source": {
    "source": "git-subdir",
    "url": "https://github.com/example-org/sdk.git",
    "path": "packages/agent-skills",
    "ref": "main",
    "sha": "<commit sha>"
  },
  "strict": false,
  "skills": [
    "./skill-a",
    "./skill-b",
    "./skill-c"
  ],
  "homepage": "https://github.com/example-org/sdk"
}
```

Each path in `skills` is relative to `source.path` and points at a directory containing a `SKILL.md`. Paths can reach deeper than a single level — for example, `["./libA/skill-1", "./libB/skill-2"]` exposes a curated subset across multiple library subdirectories. Each skill is registered as `<plugin-name>:<skill-name>` in Claude Code.

For the underlying schema, see [Strict mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces) in the marketplace documentation.

## License

Please see each linked plugin for the relevant LICENSE file.

## Documentation

For more information on developing Claude Code plugins, see the [official documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins).

name: headroom
description: Compress tool outputs, logs, files, and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM. 20% fewer tokens for coding agents, 60-95% fewer tokens for JSON, same answers. Library, proxy, MCP server.
readme_content:
Quickstart · Headroom for Teams · Install · Proof · Agents · Docs · Discord · llms.txt

AI agents / LLMs: read /llms.txt here, or fetch the live index · full docs blob.
**Headroom** (`headroom-ai` on PyPI and npm) compresses everything your AI agent reads — tool outputs, logs, RAG chunks, files, and conversation history — before it reaches the LLM. Same answers, fewer input tokens. Measured: 21–57% fewer input tokens on four agent scenarios, 90%+ on repeated JSON arrays and log lines, little on prose ([Proof](#proof-measured-token-savings)). Compression runs on your machine; no prompt or file content is sent anywhere to be compressed. ## Start here **My app calls an LLM** (Python, LangChain, LiteLLM, Agno, Strands): ```bash pip install headroom-ai ``` ```python from headroom import compress result = compress(messages, model="gpt-4o") # OpenAI or Anthropic message dicts client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4o", messages=result.messages) ``` No API key, no model download, in-process. Set `HEADROOM_OFFLINE=1` for a zero-network run. Tool and assistant messages are compressed; user messages are left alone unless you pass `compress_user_messages=True`. [FastAPI example](https://docs.headroomlabs.ai/docs/fastapi) · [API reference](https://docs.headroomlabs.ai/docs/api-reference). TypeScript apps: `npm install headroom-ai` plus the proxy (`pip install "headroom-ai[proxy]"`, `headroom proxy --port 8787`); the npm SDK sends messages to it. [TypeScript quickstart](https://docs.headroomlabs.ai/docs/quickstart) **I run coding agents** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode, Aider): ```bash uv tool install --python 3.13 "headroom-ai[all]" headroom wrap claude ``` Zero code changes. [Agent compatibility](#agent-compatibility) · [Proxy](https://docs.headroomlabs.ai/docs/proxy)


10,144 → 1,260 tokens. The same FATAL found.
## What it does - **Library** — `compress(messages)` in Python or TypeScript, inline in any app. - **Proxy** — `headroom proxy --port 8787`, zero code changes, any language. - **Agent wrap** — `headroom wrap claude|codex|grok|copilot|cursor|aider|opencode|cline|continue|goose|openhands|openclaw|vibe|omp|droid|zcode` in one command; undo with `headroom unwrap `. - **MCP server** — `headroom_compress`, `headroom_retrieve`, `headroom_stats` for any MCP client. - **Cross-agent memory** — one shared store across Claude, Codex, Gemini and Grok, with automatic dedup. - **`headroom learn`** — mines failed sessions and writes corrections to `CLAUDE.local.md` (default, gitignored), `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md` or `GROK.md`. - **Output token reduction** — trims what the model *writes back*, not only what you send. See [below](#output-token-reduction). - **Reversible (CCR)** — originals are cached locally and retrieved on demand. ## How it works ``` Your agent / app (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, LangChain, Agno, Strands, your own code…) │ prompts · tool outputs · logs · RAG results · files ▼ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Headroom (runs locally — your data stays here) │ │ ──────────────────────────────────────────────── │ │ CacheAligner → ContentRouter → CCR │ │ ├─ SmartCrusher (JSON) │ │ ├─ CodeCompressor (AST) │ │ └─ Kompress-v2-base (text, HF) │ │ │ │ Cross-agent memory · headroom learn · MCP │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ compressed prompt + retrieval tool ▼ LLM provider (Anthropic · OpenAI · Bedrock · …) ``` - **ContentRouter** detects the content type and selects a compressor for it. - **SmartCrusher / CodeCompressor / Kompress-v2-base** handle JSON, source code and prose respectively. - **CacheAligner** flags volatile content that would bust a provider KV-cache prefix. It never rewrites prompts. - **CCR** stores originals locally so the model can call `headroom_retrieve` when it needs the full text. → [Architecture](https://docs.headroomlabs.ai/docs/architecture) · [CCR](https://docs.headroomlabs.ai/docs/ccr) · [Kompress-v2-base model card](https://huggingface.co/chopratejas/kompress-v2-base) ## Get started (60 seconds) ```bash # 1 — Install uv tool install --python 3.13 "headroom-ai[all]" # CLI in a self-contained env pip install "headroom-ai[all]" # Python — ships the `headroom` CLI npm install headroom-ai # TypeScript SDK only — no CLI # 2 — Pick a mode headroom deploy # turnkey local deployment + agent config headroom wrap claude # wrap a coding agent headroom proxy --port 8787 # drop-in proxy, zero code changes # or: from headroom import compress # inline library # 3 — Check it and watch the savings headroom doctor # health check — confirms routing works headroom perf headroom dashboard # live savings (proxy must be running) ``` ### Reduce input tokens in your own app ```python from headroom import compress from openai import OpenAI messages = [{"role": "user", "content": "Analyze these results"}] result = compress(messages, model="gpt-4o") client = OpenAI() response = client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4o", messages=result.messages) print(f"Saved {result.tokens_saved} tokens ({result.compression_ratio:.0%})") ``` Launch a wrapped agent session each time, so the setup runs. `headroom wrap` starts a local proxy and launches the agent configured to route through Headroom. Add `--code-memory serena` to also install **[Serena](https://github.com/oraios/serena)** for semantic code navigation (off by default). For Claude Code, Serena is registered for the wrapped project only (as a `local`-scope MCP server in `~/.claude.json`); use `--code-memory-scope user` to make it available in every project. `headroom unwrap` removes either registration. `headroom wrap ...` is session-scoped: its proxy exits with the wrapped agent. For a proxy that survives reboots, use the turnkey `headroom deploy` command. Use `headroom install apply` when you need to choose a specific persistent service, scheduled task, Docker runtime, scope, or provider target; see the [persistent installs guide](https://docs.headroomlabs.ai/docs/persistent-installs). The `headroom` CLI ships only in the PyPI package. The npm `headroom-ai` package is the TypeScript SDK — a library you import (`import { compress } from 'headroom-ai'`) — and provides no `headroom` command. ## Proof: measured token savings Four scenarios built from real MCP server output formats, measured with the provider tokenizer and the shipped `compress()` at its default configuration. Seeded and offline, so you get the same numbers we did: ```bash uv run python benchmarks/index_proof_table.py --seed 20260902 ``` | Scenario | Before | After | Saved | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Code search (100 results) | 17,199 | 13,597 | **21%** | | SRE incident debugging | 55,957 | 24,340 | **57%** | | Codebase exploration | 58,801 | 33,895 | **42%** | | GitHub issue triage | 46,067 | 32,429 | **30%** | Savings scale with how repetitive the payload is. Repeated JSON arrays and log lines clear 90% in `benchmarks/bench_latency.py`; prose and already-dense output compress very little. Run `headroom savings` against your own traffic for the number that applies to you. Compression costs **well under a millisecond** — 0.21 ms p50 on a 10K-token JSON search result, 1.4 ms at 100K tokens — so it does not show up in agent latency. **Accuracy.** `python -m headroom.evals suite --tier 1`: | Benchmark | Category | N | Baseline | Headroom | Delta | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---| | GSM8K | Math | 100 | 0.870 | 0.870 | ±0.000 | | TruthfulQA | Factual | 100 | 0.530 | 0.560 | +0.030 | | SQuAD v2 | QA | 100 | — | 97% | at 19% compression | | BFCL | Tools | 100 | — | 97% | at 32% compression | At N=100 a delta of ±0.03 falls inside the confidence interval, so TruthfulQA shows no detectable difference rather than an improvement. [Methodology →](https://docs.headroomlabs.ai/docs/benchmarks) ## Output token reduction Everything above shrinks the prompt you **send**. You also pay for every token the model **writes back**, and on Opus-class models output costs 5× input. Much of that output is ceremony: "Great, let me…" preambles, code re-printed straight back at you, and deep reasoning spent on routine steps like reading a file. Headroom trims it from the proxy, with no change to your code: - **Verbosity steering** appends a short "be terse, don't restate context" note to the *end* of the system prompt, so your prompt cache still hits. It applies to Anthropic `/v1/messages` and to OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses`, with the same `output_shaper:*` labels on all paths. ```bash export HEADROOM_
manifest_content:
[build-system]
requires = ["maturin>=1.5,<2.0"]
build-backend = "maturin"

[project]
name = "headroom-ai"
version = "0.44.0"
description = "Compress tool outputs, logs, JSON and chat history before each LLM call. Fewer input tokens, same answers; in-process, no API key. Library, proxy and MCP server."
# PyPI renders this file; GitHub renders README.md. Keep the two in step on the
# install commands and the savings claim (README.md "Proof" is the source).
readme = "README-pypi.md"
license = "Apache-2.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [
    { name = "Headroom Contributors" }
]
maintainers = [
    { name = "Headroom Contributors" }
]
keywords = [
    "llm",
    "openai",
    "anthropic",
    "claude",
    "gpt",
    "gemini",
    "token-cost",
    "reduce-tokens",
    "input-tokens",
    "context-window",
    "token-budget",
    "tool-output",
    "tool-results",
    "chat-history",
    "trim-messages",
    "context-compression",
    "prompt-compression",
    "context-engineering",
    "agents",
    "coding-agents",
    "mcp",
    "proxy",
    "fastapi",
    "langchain",
    "litellm",
]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Operating System :: OS Independent",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering :: Artificial Intelligence",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
dependencies = [
    # Core: lightweight compression (SmartCrusher, ContentRouter, CCR, TOIN)
    "tiktoken>=0.5.0",            # Tokenizer for all compressors
    "pydantic>=2.0.0",            # Config and data models
    # Model registry, pricing and non-core providers; all lazily imported and
    # ImportError-guarded. 1.96.2 is the first litellm with prebuilt wheels for
    # Python 3.11-3.14 on Linux, macOS and Windows: older releases either reject
    # Python 3.14 (GH #956) or fall back to a Rust source build.
    "litellm>=1.96.2,<2.0",
    "click>=8.5.0",               # CLI framework; PYSEC-2026-2132 fix (command injection in click.edit())
    "rich>=13.0.0",               # Rich terminal output
    "opentelemetry-api>=1.45.2",  # CVE-2026-114603 tracestate parsing; CVE-2026-126360 traceparent ReDoS
    # AST-aware code slicing (CodeCompressor); binary wheel. 0.44.1 is excluded:
    # that PyPI release was a compromised supply-chain build shipping an
    # info-stealer `sg.exe` (Trojan:Win64/Lazy!MTB) alongside the real binary
    # (GH #2332). The `!=` keeps every other release installable, including a
    # future patched one.
    "ast-grep-cli>=0.30.0,!=0.44.1",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",                # omp wrap: parse/merge omp's models.yml registry
    "tomlkit>=0.15.2,<1.0",       # Loss-minimizing Codex config recovery
    # Verify upstream TLS through the OS trust store (macOS Keychain, Windows
    # cert store), where IT installs corporate TLS-inspection roots (Zscaler,
    # Netskope). Pure Python, no deps; the same library pip uses by default.
    "truststore>=0.10.0",
    # Not imported directly: huggingface-hub (via litellm -> tokenizers, so in
    # every install) uses it for Hub downloads. Before 1.6.0 its worker threads
    # could re-initialize or re-enter Python while the interpreter shut down
    # after a download, crashing the process at exit (SIGSEGV in
    # Py_InitializeEx, or a fatal TstateNULL error). Declared here rather than
    # as a uv constraint so the floor reaches the published wheel's metadata
    # and pip upgrades an older copy. Same platform marker as huggingface-hub's
    # own hf-xet requirement, so it never installs where hf-xet would not.
    "hf-xet>=1.6.0; platform_machine == 'AMD64' or platform_machine == 'aarch64' or platform_machine == 'amd64' or platform_machine == 'arm64' or platform_machine == 'x86_64'",
    # Not imported directly: litellm, huggingface-hub and torch use it.
    # CVE-2026-112907/112913/112940 are fixed in 4.2.1, but litellm 1.106 caps
    # filelock <4, so without this floor pip picks that litellm and 3.32.7;
    # with it pip takes litellm 1.103.7 (uv.lock has 1.101.0). Declared here so
    # the floor reaches pip installs.
    "filelock>=4.2.1",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Proxy server (most common install: pip install headroom-ai[proxy])
proxy = [
    "fastapi>=0.100.0",
    "uvicorn>=0.23.0,<1.0",
    # LiteLLM provider backends (e.g. openrouter) expect orjson at runtime but
    # litellm only declares it under its own [proxy] extra (GH #2056).
    "orjson>=3.9.14; platform_python_implementation != 'PyPy'",
    "httpx[http2]>=0.24.0",
    "openai>=2.14.0",             # OpenAI API format support
    # SDK 2 constructor-callback API (GH #2658). 2.2.0 fixes CVE-2026-59951
    # and CVE-2026-116684/116685/116686, which affect 2.0

name: a2ui
description: Open-source generative UI framework: agents stream layout data, and apps render it with native components in React, Angular, Lit, Flutter, SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose.
readme_content: # A2UI **Build delightful, fast, reliable agentic experiences** A2UI (Agent-to-User Interface) is an open-source generative UI framework, complete with a protocol optimized for streaming dynamic user interfaces at low latency, native renderers for web and mobile frameworks, and agent SDKs in several popular languages. With A2UI, your agents can communicate with your users using natively rendered widgets, in addition to text. _Examples of UI compositions that A2UI can express._ ## Quick links - [Main website](https://a2ui.org). - Try it in your browser using [A2UI Composer](https://a2ui-project.github.io/composer/). - [Supported renderers](https://a2ui.org/reference/renderers/). - [Supported agents](https://a2ui.org/reference/agents/). - [Protocol specification](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/). ## Introduction Large language models (LLMs) and decision models (e.g. [Jev](https://docs.typesafe.ai/)) excel at creating text and code and at making fast decisions on top of raw structured data (e.g. JSON). A2UI gives these models a specialized vocabulary for expressing user interfaces. A2UI expresses UI using _data_, not code. A schema for the data exchanged between the agent and the renderer enforces strict capability boundaries for the agent, keeping agent-generated experiences safe and aligned with the business requirements of your application. A _core library_, a _native framework adapter_, and a _catalog of components_ provide access to native components and form the building blocks that the agent _composes_ into a final user experience, making the result expressive and high-performance. ## When to use A2UI Use A2UI when any of the following apply to your application: - Parts of your application are agent- and/or server-driven. By design, A2UI supports remote rendering. - You want the UI to be composed dynamically, tailored to the user's immediate need. Instead of making your users navigate through multiple screens to solve their problems, have the agent build the right flow of UI that guides users directly to solutions. - You need the highest performance and visual fidelity. A2UI renders UI using the framework of your choice, typically one that the host app itself is written in. WebViews or HTML are not required. - The same agent streams UI to multiple platforms or frameworks, such as Flutter, React, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose. A2UI helps keep the user experience compatible and consistent across all screens. - The agent is remote, third-party, or operates across a trust boundary. For example, the agent must not be able to handle certain kinds of data (credit card/account numbers, PII, financial data). A2UI helps enforce the trust boundary and protect your app's critical functionality from hallucinations using a strict schema, and by expressing UI using validated data rather than executable code. ## A2UI core philosophy We develop A2UI under the guidance of the following core principles: - **Security first**: The app developer controls what the agent can and cannot do in the app. A2UI provides a framework for specifying and enforcing the necessary guardrails, such as expressing UI as data, validating inputs and outputs against a schema, and disallowing arbitrary executable code. Every capability granted to the agent is either a safe standard capability built into the framework, or a capability explicitly granted by the app developer. - **Model-friendly and server-driven**: The A2UI protocol is designed to be efficiently generated by language and decision models and transported over the network, and to support progressive rendering (or "streaming") for a responsive user experience. An agent can adapt the UI based on where the user takes the conversation. A2UI supports swappable inference formats, so you can tailor inference to specific models and use cases. - **Native rendering and portability**: A2UI renders UI using the framework native to your app, with renderers for many major UI frameworks. No need to change frameworks unless required for other reasons. ## Architecture A2UI's architecture is made of multiple layers spanning the full stack that connects the agent to the application: 1. **Inference**: An agent (typically backed by a language or a decision model) instructed by an A2UI skill (created using an A2UI Agent SDK) generates the description of UI and data using an appropriate inference format (e.g. A2UI Express, or a decision tree). 2. **Transport**: An A2UI Agent SDK, embedded in a larger agent architecture, parses and validates the model's output, expands macros, and converts the UI to the wire-stable _A2UI Transport_ protocol messages, which are sent to the renderer. 3. **Rendering**: A renderer is made of an _A2UI Core_ library (e.g. the `@a2ui/web_core` npm package, or `a2ui_core` Dart package), a UI framework adapter (e.g. `@a2ui/react` React adapter, or `a2ui_flutter` Flutter adapter), and a widget catalog. The core library parses the incoming messages and creates a framework-agnostic in-memory representation of the UI and data. The framework adapter maps the in-memory representation to concrete framework-specific UI widgets. The widget catalog provides access to the widgets the agent is allowed to compose. ## Getting started Pick the path that matches where you want to start: | Path | What you get | Time | | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | | 🍜 **[Quickstart](https://a2ui.org/quickstart/)** | A full-stack A2UI app with a backend and frontend. Learn A2UI end-to-end and customize to your use case. | ~5 min | | 🎨 **[A2UI Composer](https://a2ui-project.github.io/composer/)** | Generate A2UI JSON from a visual editor and paste it into any agent prompt — no install required. | ~1 min | | 🎬 **[A2UI Theater](https://a2ui-composer.ag-ui.com/theater)** | Step through pre-built A2UI streaming scenarios across Lit, React, and Angular renderers — no install required. | ~1 min | ## Packages These packages are developed in this repository. Packages marked "Not published yet" can be used from source. ### Python | Package | Description | Version | | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | [a2ui-core](python/a2ui_core/) | Protocol messages, data model, data binding, expression evaluation, and catalog validation. | [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/a2ui-core.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-core/) | | [a2ui-agent-sdk](python/a2ui_agent/) | Agent SDK: negotiates catalogs, generates prompts and skills, and compiles model output into A2UI. | [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/a2ui-agent-sdk.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/a2ui-agent-sdk/) | | {
  "name": "a2ui-workspace",
  "private": true,
  "packageManager": "yarn@4.13.0",
  "workspaces": [
    "catalogs/*",
    "typescript/*",
    "typescript/agents/*",
    "typescript/catalogs/*",
    "typescript/core/*",
    "typescript/renderers/*",
    "typescript/renderers/angular/*",
    "typescript/renderers/lit/*",
    "typescript/renderers/react/*",
    "samples/agent/node/*",
    "samples/client/angular",
    "samples/client/angular/projects/*",
    "samples/client/lit",
    "samples/client/lit/*",
    "samples/client/react/*",
    "samples/vegachart",
    "specification/*/test",
    "tools/*",
    "!**/dist"
  ],
  "scripts": {
    "build:all": "yarn workspaces foreach -A -p --topological-dev run build",
    "test:all": "yarn workspaces foreach -A -p --topological-dev run test",
    "lint:all": "yarn workspaces foreach -A -p --topological-dev run lint",
    "lint:deps": "syncpack list-mismatches",
    "lint:fix:all": "yarn workspaces foreach -A -p --topological-dev run lint:fix",
    "format:all": "prettier --config .prettierrc --write .",
    "format:check:all": "prettier --config .prettierrc --check .",
    "clean:all": "yarn workspaces foreach -A -p run clean"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "google-artifactregistry-auth": "^3.5.0",
    "prettier": "^3.8.4",
    "syncpack": "^13.0.0",
    "typescript": "5.9.3",
    "wireit": "^0.15.0-pre.2"
  },
  "resolutions": {
    "@playwright/test": "1.58.1",
    "playwright": "1.58.1",

    "@a2ui/web_core": "workspace:*",

    "@a2ui/markdown-it": "workspace:*",
    "@angular/core": "^21.2.5",

    "@angular/compiler": "^21.2.5",

    "@angular/cdk": "^21.2.5",

    "undici": "7.28.0",
    "dompurify": "3.4.11",
    "piscina": "5.2.0",
